input.message:
All 17 `/tools` routes (the `/nxm/tools` hub plus 16 tool pages) now load on the new site and the tools I ran return real results. Every route returns 200, and its title and description match the live page. I ran seven of the tools in the browser (Base64, DNS, latency, Minecraft status, domain generator, password generator, what-is-my-IP) plus the size calculator; the other eight tools only got a load check. No commits and no deploys; my `tsc` output is clean.

## What was checked
- **SEO on all 17:** canonical is the production route. Each tool page has FAQPage (matching the live question count), BreadcrumbList (Home › Free tools › tool), and the same WebApplication entry the live page emits (the Minecraft page gets its SoftwareApplication verbatim). The hub has the live ItemList plus a BreadcrumbList. Organization and WebSite come from the root layout, as on live.
- **Tools run against the live endpoints:**
  - **Base64:** encodes correctly.
  - **DNS:** `nxeon.cloud` returned real A, MX, TXT, NS and SOA records.
  - **Latency test:** the unchanged live component, same `/api/tools/ping` endpoint; it completed 15/15 real round trips with average, best, worst and jitter. The numbers are high on dev only because :3033 is heavily loaded.
  - **Minecraft status:** `mc.hypixel.net` came back online with real player count, MOTD, version and latency. One earlier "Failed to fetch" was the dev server restarting mid-request; the endpoint works when called directly.
- **Size calculator**, driven in the browser across several workloads:
  - Minecraft vanilla, 10 players: the Minecraft 4 GB/20-slot tier at $8.99 with a game deploy link, plus the Standard VPS at $12.99 as "Or self-manage it".
  - WordPress at maximum traffic: Pro VPS, $20.99.
  - DayZ (no active game tiers): Starter VPS.
  - Minecraft modded at 60 players, and Palworld: nothing is big enough, so it shows the closest managed tier and the Max VPS, each tagged "Closest", with plain notes saying so.
  - All deploy links come from `deployHref` and all prices from the live plan data.
  - Product links go to `/nxm` pages where they exist.
- **Console:** no page errors on repeat runs; the one transient 404 and a hydration warning from the shared footer's `<details>` didn't come back.

## Fixes from this pass
- The final CTA band was unstyled on both templates; I added the design's `.wh-final` styles.
- Mobile at 390px:
  - Hub stats stay in three columns.
  - The category filter is compacted.
  - The tagline in the tool bar is hidden.
  - The size calculator's deploy buttons wrap and read "Deploy this server".
- Size calculator: the "the pick is a Cloud VPS" note now only appears when a VPS actually fits.

Screenshots were checked at 1440 (hub, size calculator, Base64, DNS, latency, Minecraft, domain generator, password, my-IP) and 390 (hub, size calculator, Base64). I deleted them afterwards to save disk; `/tmp/claude-0/-root/ec6fa978-d80b-4147-9982-eea470598e2c/scratchpad/tools/` keeps two samples (`v-f1.jpg`, the lower half of a tool page at 1440, and `v-m1.jpg`, a tool panel at 390) and the scripts, about 100 KB.

## How it's built
- **Hub `/tools`:** a native page with a hero, stats, a sticky search box and category filter, grouped tool cards (the domain generator is featured first, as on live) and the CTA. Hero and category text are read from the live `/tools` page at request time; cards come from the live catalogue in `lib/tools/catalog.ts`.
- **One template for all 16 tools:** hero with facts, the tool in a glass panel, explainer and how-to, FAQ, related tools, and a CTA with a real "from" price (VPS plans, or Minecraft tiers on the Minecraft page).
  - The live pages are the source for everything on these pages, read at request time (not copied): each page's title/description and the text it passes to its layout, converted to HTML. If it finds something it can't convert, it errors rather than rendering a gap.
  - The Minecraft page is a custom landing, so its explainer, FAQ and structured data are read from its own markup. Its hero line and CTA text aren't exported, so those two strings are copied from `ToolLanding.tsx`.
- **Mounting the live tools:** `app/nxm/tools/layout.tsx` renders a small client component that loads the page's tool on demand and places it into the panel. 15 live components run unchanged on the same `/api/tools/*` endpoints. The restyle is CSS limited to the tool panel; it also undoes the design's page-wide resets inside the tool, which would otherwise override the live components' own styles. No change to `NxmPage` was needed.
- **Size calculator:** a new Aurora UI on the live sizing model in `lib/tools/server-sizing.ts`. It recommends from the active VPS plans and the matching game's active tiers. The workload-to-game mapping is taken from the existing game-page routes, not hardcoded.

## Files
- **New:**
  - `tools/nxm/native/tools/{body.html,page.css,page.js,meta.json}`
  - `tools/nxm/native/tools-tool/{body.html,page.css,meta.json}`
  - `tools/nxm/wire/tools.py`, `tools/nxm/wire/tools_tool.py`
  - `tools/nxm/routes/tools-tool.json`
  - `app/nxm/_data/tools.ts`, `app/nxm/_data/tools-tool.ts`, `app/nxm/_data/tools-live.ts`
  - `app/nxm/_components/ToolMount.tsx`, `app/nxm/_components/ToolSizeCalculator.tsx`
  - `app/nxm/tools/layout.tsx`
- **Generated:** `app/nxm/_pages/{tools,tools-tool}/*`, `app/nxm/tools/page.tsx`, `app/nxm/tools/<16 slugs>/page.tsx`, and `app/nxm/_pages/scripts.ts` (rebuilt from the folder listing). The port audit shows both pages "wired" with no stale prices.
- **Shared, small additions only:** two `ROUTES` lines in `tools/nxm/nxmlib.py` (`tools`, `tools-tool`) and a `/tools` entry in `app/nxm/_seo/registry.ts` (live title and description, crumb "Free tools").

## Didn't fit
- Links inside the live components (for example "Nxeon Minecraft hosting", "deploy a low-latency NVMe VPS") point to live routes rather than `/nxm`. This only matters on staging.
- The tools appear only after JavaScript loads; a skeleton shows until then.
- `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` isn't updated because it's shared and nothing is committed yet.

## Decisions for you or the owner
1. **The live Minecraft status landing shows testimonials that look made up** (`TOOL_REVIEWS` in `components/marketing/tooltemplate/data.ts`). I kept them off the new page; the live page still shows them.
2. **The sizing model disagrees with what we sell.** It asks for 18 GB for 8 Palworld players, while we sell a 16 GB/32-player tier; for modded Minecraft at 60 players it asks for 21 GB. Should game workloads use checkout's own curve in `lib/game-player-recommend.ts` instead?
3. **Game workloads show two options.** The size calculator offers a managed tier first and a Cloud VPS as "Or self-manage it". Keep both, or show one?
4. **The live hub hero says "no tracking"**, but the site sets analytics cookies. That copy is read straight from the live page, so it needs fixing there.

The restyle is CSS limited to the tool panel; it also undoes the design's page-wide resets inside the tool, which would otherwise override the live components' own styles. No change to `NxmPage` was needed.
- **Size calculator:** a new Aurora UI on the live sizing model in `lib/tools/server-sizing.ts`. It recommends from the active VPS plans and the matching game's active tiers. The workload-to-game mapping is taken from the existing game-page routes, not hardcoded.

## Files
- **New:**
  - `tools/nxm/native/tools/{body.html,page.css,page.js,meta.json}`
  - `tools/nxm/native/tools-tool/{body.html,page.css,meta.json}`
  - `tools/nxm/wire/tools.py`, `tools/nxm/wire/tools_tool.py`
  - `tools/nxm/routes/tools-tool.json`
  - `app/nxm/_data/tools.ts`, `app/nxm/_data/tools-tool.ts`, `app/nxm/_data/tools-live.ts`
  - `app/nxm/_components/ToolMount.tsx`, `app/nxm/_components/ToolSizeCalculator.tsx`
  - `app/nxm/tools/layout.tsx`
- **Generated:** `app/nxm/_pages/{tools,tools-tool}/*`, `app/nxm/tools/page.tsx`, `app/nxm/tools/<16 slugs>/page.tsx`, and `app/nxm/_pages/scripts.ts` (rebuilt from the folder listing). The port audit shows both pages "wired" with no stale prices.
- **Shared, small additions only:** two `ROUTES` lines in `tools/nxm/nxmlib.py` (`tools`, `tools-tool`) and a `/tools` entry in `app/nxm/_seo/registry.ts` (live title and description, crumb "Free tools").

## Didn't fit
- Links inside the live components (for example "Nxeon Minecraft hosting", "deploy a low-latency NVMe VPS") point to live routes rather than `/nxm`. This only matters on staging.
- The tools appear only after JavaScript loads; a skeleton shows until then.
- `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` isn't updated because it's shared and nothing is committed yet.

## Decisions for you or the owner
1. **The live Minecraft status landing shows testimonials that look made up** (`TOOL_REVIEWS` in `components/marketing/tooltemplate/data.ts`). I kept them off the new page; the live page still shows them.
2. **The sizing model disagrees with what we sell.** It asks for 18 GB for 8 Palworld players, while we sell a 16 GB/32-player tier; for modded Minecraft at 60 players it asks for 21 GB. Should game workloads use checkout's own curve in `lib/game-player-recommend.ts` instead?
3. **Game workloads show two options.** The size calculator offers a managed tier first and a Cloud VPS as "Or self-manage it". Keep both, or show one?
4. **The live hub hero says "no tracking"**, but the site sets analytics cookies. That copy is read straight from the live page, so it needs fixing there.

All 17 `/tools` routes now work on the new site: the hub plus 16 tool pages. Every route returns 200 and its title and description match the live page. Nothing was committed or deployed.

**What I checked**
- **SEO:** every page has the same structured data as its live page, plus breadcrumbs. Canonicals point at the production routes.
- **Tools I actually ran:**
  - **DNS:** a lookup of `nxeon.cloud` returned its real records.
  - **Minecraft status:** a check of `mc.hypixel.net` came back online with the real player count.
  - **Latency test:** completed all 15 real round trips to the live ping endpoint. The numbers were high only because the dev server is heavily loaded.
  - **Also run:** Base64, the domain generator, the password generator and what-is-my-IP.
- **Not run:** the other eight tools only got a page-load check.
- **Size calculator:** I clicked through several workloads.
  - Minecraft with 10 players recommends the 4 GB/20-slot game server at $8.99, with the $12.99 Standard VPS as the self-managed option.
  - WordPress at maximum traffic recommends the $20.99 Pro VPS.
  - When nothing is big enough (modded Minecraft at 60 players, Palworld), it shows the closest game server and the largest VPS and says plainly that neither fully fits.
  - Every price and deploy link comes from the live plan data.

**Fixes from this pass**
- The final call-to-action section was unstyled on both page types; it now has the design's styling.
- On phones (390px wide), the hub stats, the category filter, the tool header and the size calculator's buttons are tightened up. The calculator's button now reads "Deploy this server".

I checked screenshots on desktop for most of the pages and on mobile for three of them, then deleted most of them to save disk; about 100 KB is left.

**Known gaps**
- Links inside the live tools, such as "Nxeon Minecraft hosting", point to the live site rather than the staging preview. This only matters on staging.
- Each tool appears only after JavaScript loads; a loading placeholder shows until then.
- `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` isn't updated because it's a shared file and nothing is committed yet.

**Decisions for you or the owner**
1. **Made-up testimonials on the live site:** the Minecraft status page shows two ("mika.exe", "Jordan P.") that look invented. I left them off the new page, but the live page still shows them.
2. **Calculator sizing vs. what we sell:** the calculator's sizing disagrees with our game plans. For 8 Palworld players it asks for 18 GB, while we sell a 16 GB plan rated for 32 players. Should game workloads use checkout's own player-count sizing instead?
3. **One option or two:** for games, the size calculator shows a managed game server first and a VPS second. Keep both, or show only one?
